system.name: MESSI
system.one_liner: a model-based testing system that encodes BGP behavior (decision process, route filtering, regex matching) in the Zen solver-aided language to systematically generate test cases for BGP implementations

content.key_idea: To build a positive test case exercising DFA state 5, MESSI concatenates two paths: P1 (1→3→5) from the start to the target state, and P2 (5→7→9→10) from the target onward to an accepting state.
content.reading_order: starts at state 1, follows dotted maroon P1 up through state 3 to target state 5, then dashed brown P2 through 7 and 9 to accepting state 10; plain black edges show the rest.

encoding.emphasis: colouring only three of the eleven states and drawing only two path-segments in a non-solid style isolates exactly the path MESSI needs, letting it stand out against the otherwise plain black-and-white DFA

summary: Figure 7 shows how MESSI's coverage algorithm builds a positive test example that exercises a chosen DFA state, using state 5 as the illustration. Among the DFA's eleven states, 1 is the start state, 5 is the target to be covered, and 10 is the sole accepting state. MESSI first searches for a path P1 (dotted maroon) from the start state to the target, here 1→3→5; it then searches for a second path P2 (dashed brown/orange) from that target onward to an accepting state, here 5→7→9→10. Concatenating the two paths, 1→3→5→7→9→10, yields one complete run of the automaton that both passes through state 5 and ends in acceptance. The rest of the DFA's transitions, including self-loops on states 8 and 11, are drawn in plain black and play no part in this particular example.
